note: Taiwan, read in the Immigration Act (入出國及移民法, as amended 28 June 2023), the Nationality Act (國籍法) and the Employment Service Act (就業服務法), as the Ministry of Justice's law database serves them (read 2026-10-30). A foreigner employed in Taiwan with a work permit for artistic and performing work (the work engine's route) has residence and applies within 30 days of entry for the Alien Resident Certificate, valid at most three years from approval (no single term is kept), tied to the employer's permit. After five years' lawful continuous residence with 183 days a year, a foreigner who is of age, of good conduct and self-supporting may ask for permanent residence; a first prize in an internationally recognised competition in culture or the arts, or being a needed senior professional, allows it without the years. A permanent resident may ask for a work permit directly, without an employer, and free of the listed categories (read as any work). A spouse of a citizen or resident may reside to join them; whether they may work without a permit was not read here, so the game reads work for a sponsor. Naturalisation asks five years' lawful residence with 183 days a year, so the years count. Fees (the ARC's and the permanent residence certificate's) and decision times were not read: the National Immigration Agency's fee rules were not reached.
